The evidence suggests that Promethazine, as part of the phenothiazine class, binds to Calm1, a protein involved in neural regulation. This binding is supported by the presence of Promethazine in the phenothiazine family, which includes Fluphenazine, another compound that interacts with Calm1. The mechanism of action appears to involve a direct interaction between Promethazine and Calm1, potentially modulating its function in the nervous system. The low common ancestor relationship between Promethazine and Fluphenazine further reinforces the notion of a shared biological pathway, suggesting that the interaction between these compounds and Calm1 may be conserved across the phenothiazine class. The integrated evidence supports a mechanistic link between Promethazine and Calm1, particularly through its role in affecting the nervous system and its classification as a tertiary amino compound.
